name: Theodore von Kármán
summary: Hungarian-American engineer and physicist active in aeronautics, astronautics, and rock mechanics.

name: Budapest
summary: Capital city of Hungary, birthplace of von Kármán.

name: Aachen
summary: City in Germany where von Kármán directed the Aeronautical Institute and died.

aliases: Budapest University of Technology and Economics
name: Royal Joseph University
summary: University in Budapest where von Kármán graduated as a mechanical engineer.

name: University of Göttingen
summary: German university where von Kármán worked as an assistant to Ludwig Prandtl.

name: Aeronautical Institute at Aachen
summary: Institute directed by von Kármán starting in 1912.

name: Austro-Hungarian Army
summary: Military force in which von Kármán served from 1915 to 1918.

name: United States of America
summary: Country to which von Kármán emigrated in 1930.

name: Hungarian Society of Engineers and Architects
summary: Professional society where von Kármán first presented his triaxial test results.

name: Hungarian Academy of Sciences
summary: Academy where von Kármán repeated his triaxial test presentation.

name: Krupp
summary: Company in Essen that produced von Kármán's triaxial test chamber.

name: Essen
summary: City in Germany where Krupp produced the triaxial cell.

name: Ludwig Prandtl
summary: Professor at the University of Göttingen and supervisor of von Kármán.

name: Franz Joseph
summary: King of Hungary who granted nobility to von Kármán's family.

name: The Bomb
summary: First triaxial test chamber designed by von Kármán for investigating brittle rock behavior.

name: Journal of Hungarian Engineers and Architects
summary: Journal where von Kármán's triaxial test results were first published in Hungarian.

name: Z. Verhandl. Deut. Ingr.
summary: Journal where von Kármán's triaxial test results were published in German.

name: E. Heyn
summary: Professor of geology in Heidelberg who pointed out plastic deformation in brittle rocks.
